transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light gardening after 1 week, as long as it’s not heavy work. Please avoid strenuous exercise and heavy lifting for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops or gel before your operation, it’s safe to continue using them unless you were told otherwise. If you’re running out, your GP should be able to provide more.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate that information. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light can be normal while your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it’s mild and things just seem brighter, wear sunglasses outside.

But significant pain with bright light, or severe light sensitivity, especially with a red and painful eye, is not normal and may need checking.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after the operation. It should improve quickly and settle over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting worse, it may need to be checked.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass
